blocks.text: Cable car above the bay and hills of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
Rio de Janeiro: cable car above the waterfront city

After breakfast, set out on an eight-hour sightseeing tour with lunch at a traditional Brazilian churrascaria. It’s one of the busiest days of the trip. You’ll spend the day off the motorbikes, exploring downtown Rio, Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain.

The route takes you through central Rio, past modern and colonial architecture and Candelária Church, before reaching the foot of Corcovado. Take the train up through the rainforest to the Christ the Redeemer statue at an elevation of about 700 metres. From the viewing platform, you can see across the city to the Botanical Garden, Maracanã Stadium, Guanabara Bay and Sugarloaf Mountain.

After descending, head to Praia Vermelha, or Red Beach. The cable car takes you up to Urca and then to Sugarloaf Mountain. The mountain’s name is often linked to its resemblance to a loaf of sugar. Another possible origin is the local term Pau-nh-acuqua, meaning ‘high hill’. From the top, you can see the city, the sea and the mountain ranges around the bay, with an especially clear view of the coastline towards Copacabana. Return to the hotel after the tour.
